scope: KNOT cryptographic core (include/ccts/), not modified by the assurance layer
policy: Findings are documented and reproduced by CI (status known-fail); the assurance layer does not alter the core. A finding that stops reproducing makes CI report xpass so this registry is updated deliberately.

severity_scale.high: memory-safety, crash, hang or incorrect output reachable from untrusted input, or a property a deployment would rely on
severity_scale.medium: design-level deviation from what a production verifier should provide; no memory-safety impact

findings.title: unsigned __int128 in ntt.hpp: 32-bit targets and MSVC do not compile
findings.observed: error: expected primary-expression before '(' token (no __int128 on i386); also -Wpedantic warning on 64-bit
findings.required_core_change: portable 64x64->128 multiplication mod the Goldilocks prime (e.g. 32-bit limb arithmetic or a compiler-specific fallback)

findings.title: ByteReader::bytes() copies an attacker-controlled length without a bounds check (heap-buffer-overflow read)
findings.observed: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ in ByteReader::bytes() via deserialize_signature_packed (also reachable from PublicKey::deserialize for support_seed/payload)
findings.required_core_change: bounds-check n against remaining bytes in ByteReader::bytes() (and make u8/u16/u32 failures rejections rather than exceptions-by-accident)
findings.adapter_mitigation: knot_adapter::signature_from_bytes_* and validate_public_key_bytes validate framing before calling the core

findings.title: verify() accepts non-canonical (scaled) u and v: signature malleability
findings.reproduction: production/tests/negative_test.cpp: scale u by any nonzero scalar; verify still returns true
findings.expected: a production verifier accepts exactly the canonical projective representatives the signer emits (strong unforgeability)
findings.observed: (q-1)^2 distinct encodings of every signature verify; EUF-CMA unaffected, SUF-CMA not provided
findings.required_core_change: reject u/v whose first nonzero coordinate is not 1 (matches the signer's projectivize())

findings.title: deserialize_signature_packed accepts non-canonical radix payloads
findings.reproduction: production/tests/negative_test.cpp: add q^n to the packed integer (fits in the same byte length); raw deserializer yields the same (u, v)
findings.observed: multiple byte strings decode to the same signature and verify
findings.required_core_change: reject payload integers >= q^n (re-encode and compare, or check the leading limb)
findings.adapter_mitigation: signature_from_bytes_packed re-serializes and requires byte equality

findings.title: PublicKey::deserialize performs no structural validation: heap overflow write, unbounded allocation, division by zero
findings.observed: (a) TRI branch: nz read from the bit stream is not checked against k+1 -> heap-buffer-overflow WRITE at scheme.hpp:370 (AddressSanitizer); (b) dense branch: n1,n2,n3 from the header are multiplied and allocated without limit or consistency check against k -> multi-terabyte allocation attempt / OOM kill (ASan: 0x8340003840000-byte request); (c) k and q are not validated: non-prime q, q <= 4k, q >= 2^16 and q < 3 are accepted (Field asserts q >= 3 only in debug builds; q = 0 happens to be rejected later by verify's element range check); (d) element values are not checked to be < q, so non-canonical public keys are accepted
findings.required_core_change: validate k, q (prime, q > 4k, q < 2^16), tensor dimensions against k, element ranges, nz < k+1, and payload length before allocating
findings.adapter_mitigation: knot_adapter::validate_public_key_bytes performs all of these checks

findings.title: Core does not compile cleanly under strict diagnostics
findings.required_core_change: explicit casts / index types; none of the warnings indicate a functional defect on the tested platforms

findings.title: Signing has secret-dependent control flow and memory access (not constant-time)
findings.reproduction: valgrind --error-exitcode=99 --xml=yes --xml-file=out.xml build/production/valgrind/ctgrind_knot tensor_reference/k=8 ; build/production/gcc-release/dudect_knot (KNOT_DUDECT_SAMPLES=20000 for the long run)
findings.expected: no secret-dependent branches or addresses in sign()
findings.observed: Valgrind memcheck with secret-key bytes marked undefined reports 88 UninitCondition (secret-dependent conditional jumps) and 13-14 UninitValue events during a single sign() at k=8 in each of tensor_reference, chord_structured and tri_chord (ci-artifacts/results/sidechannel-ctgrind-*-report.json). The dudect-style Welch t-test on sign() with two keys does NOT resolve a timing difference at 500 samples per class (max |t| <= 3.7 < 4.5); the nightly 20000-sample run is the relevant statistical evidence and has not yet been evaluated. The verify() valid-vs-salt-flipped experiment shows |t| = 7.4 on tensor_reference (early rejection on public data, informational).
findings.required_core_change: constant-time field arithmetic (branchless reduction, Fermat inversion without early exits is already branchless but pow's loop over the public exponent is fine; the data-dependent parts are the sphere/zero-set partition in vwz_preimage, the monomial permutation application, and rejection sampling), or an explicit non-CT statement in the deployment profile

findings.title: SHAKE256 implementation is byte-order dependent: wrong output on big-endian hosts
findings.observed: SHAKE256 KATs fail on s390x (big-endian); consequently every DRBG output, key, digest and signature differs from little-endian hosts and from the KAT corpus
findings.required_core_change: load/store lanes as little-endian 64-bit words (byte-wise assembly) instead of aliasing the state array

findings.title: derive_support relies on assert() for t <= 2k+1: abort in default builds, infinite loop under NDEBUG
findings.expected: a TRI public key with t > 2k+1 is rejected
findings.observed: assertion failure (SIGABRT) in the default build; with -DNDEBUG the rejection-sampling loop can never collect t distinct indices and never terminates
findings.required_core_change: validate t (k+2 <= t <= 2k+1) and w in PublicKey::deserialize before deriving the support
